newsitem.title: BRAZIL: CVRD says gold, copper finds not new.
newsitem.headline: CVRD says gold, copper finds not new.

text.p: State mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) told Brazilian financial markets it had already disclosed gold and copper finds in northern Brazil that were reported Tuesday in a local newspaper.

In a statement to Brazil bolsas, the company said it had reported to markets on Oct 23 the same gold and copper mineralization described in an O Estado de S. Paulo report that sent shares soaring more than four percent in early trade.
"At the time, we reported mineralization in two drill holes out of a total of six, and the drilling of six other holes," the statement said.
The statement followed a request by Sao Paulo stock exchange for more information on the news report.
It said the company has so far completed 12 holes, of which five showed traces of gold and copper, and the results are "promising."
Four holes are now underway, with 30 others scheduled to be drilled, and the economic feasibility of the projects will only be decided when drilling is concluded.
No pre-feasibility study has been prepared yet, it said.

Estado said in a lead page one story that CVRD had made a "historic" find of rich gold and copper deposits in Carajas in Para state near the existing Igarape Bahia gold mine and the Salobo gold, copper and silver project.
